## Preparation


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

input_file <- "../data/cleaned/04-all_metrics_sample-level_CLEANED.csv"

# EDIT: These are the exact column names expected in your CSV.
id_col <- "sample_id"
site_col <- "site_number"
metric_cols <- c("p450", "sod", "condition_index", "shell")

# Outputs will be written alongside this Quarto document.
output_dir <- "../data/adjusted"
#dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

### Load data

```{r}
if (file.exists(input_file)) {
  biomarker_raw <- read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  data_origin <- "USER CSV"
} else {
  set.seed(2026)
  biomarker_raw <- tibble(
    sample_id = sprintf("DEMO_%03d", 1:80),
    site_number = rep(1:20, each = 4),
    p450 = rlnorm(80, meanlog = 0.1, sdlog = 0.6),
    sod = rlnorm(80, meanlog = 2.0, sdlog = 0.45),
    condition_index = rnorm(80, mean = 9, sd = 1.2),
    shell = rnorm(80, mean = 1.8, sd = 0.25)
  )
  biomarker_raw$p450[c(7, 44)] <- c(16, 0.02)
  biomarker_raw$sod[30] <- 65
  biomarker_raw$condition_index[61] <- 16
  biomarker_raw$shell[12] <- 3.2
  biomarker_raw$p450[18] <- NA_real_
  data_origin <- "SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION — NOT RESEARCH DATA"
}

cat("Data source:", data_origin, "\n")

required_cols <- c(id_col, site_col, metric_cols)
missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(biomarker_raw))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("Missing expected columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". Edit the configuration in Section 1.")
}

# Confirm an unambiguous sample identifier before inspecting outliers.
if (anyNA(biomarker_raw[[id_col]]) || anyDuplicated(biomarker_raw[[id_col]]) > 0) {
  stop("Sample IDs must be non-missing and unique. Check whether you need a composite ID.")
}

if (!all(vapply(biomarker_raw[metric_cols], is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
  stop("All selected measurement columns must be numeric. Check import and units.")
}

biomarker_long <- biomarker_raw %>%
  rename(sample_id_work = all_of(id_col), site_work = all_of(site_col)) %>%
  mutate(sample_id_work = as.character(sample_id_work),
         site_work = as.character(site_work)) %>%
  select(sample_id_work, site_work, all_of(metric_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metric_cols), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

kable(biomarker_long %>% count(metric, name = "n_records"))
```

## Audit values (before calling anything an outlier)

```{r}
value_audit <- biomarker_long %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(value)),
    n_nonfinite = sum(!is.finite(value) & !is.na(value)),
    n_zero = sum(value == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_negative = sum(value < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = if (all(is.na(value))) NA_real_ else min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = if (all(is.na(value))) NA_real_ else max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
kable(value_audit, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
biomarker_long %>%
  filter(is.finite(value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 18, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Untransformed distributions", x = "Measurement", y = "Number of samples") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
biomarker_long %>%
  filter(is.finite(value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = value, x = metric)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Individual measurements alongside boxplots", x = NULL, y = "Measurement") +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Flag potential outliers, per metric

We calculate two complementary descriptive rules over **all samples for each metric**:

- **Tukey IQR fences:** below Q1 − 1.5 × IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 × IQR.
- **Modified z-score:** 0.6745 × (value − median) / MAD (where MAD is the median *unscaled* absolute deviation); flag absolute scores greater than 3.5.

These are *screening conventions*, not hypothesis tests and not automatic deletion criteria. If the MAD is zero, its score is undefined and is left missing. A metric may be flagged by one rule and not another.

```{r}
metric_reference <- biomarker_long %>%
  filter(is.finite(value)) %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(
    n_valid = n(),
    q1 = quantile(value, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    q3 = quantile(value, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    median_value = median(value),
    mad_raw = median(abs(value - median(value))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(iqr = q3 - q1,
         lower_fence = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
         upper_fence = q3 + 1.5 * iqr)

outlier_audit <- biomarker_long %>%
  left_join(metric_reference, by = "metric") %>%
  mutate(
    flag_iqr = if_else(is.finite(value),
                       value < lower_fence | value > upper_fence,
                       FALSE),
    modified_z = if_else(is.finite(value) & !is.na(mad_raw) & mad_raw > 0,
                         0.6745 * (value - median_value) / mad_raw,
                         NA_real_),
    flag_mad = coalesce(abs(modified_z) > 3.5, FALSE),
    flag_any = flag_iqr | flag_mad,
    review_status = if_else(flag_any, "Needs investigation", "Not flagged"),
    # Flag-based exclusion below is a SENSITIVITY SCENARIO, not a QC decision.
    sensitivity_exclude = flag_any
  )

kable(metric_reference, digits = 3)
```

### Locate the specific sample and metric

```{r}
flagged_samples <- outlier_audit %>%
  filter(flag_any) %>%
  arrange(metric, desc(abs(modified_z))) %>%
  select(sample_id_work, site_work, metric, value,
         lower_fence, upper_fence, modified_z,
         flag_iqr, flag_mad, review_status)

kable(flagged_samples, digits = 3,
      caption = "Every flagged observation, linked to its sample ID and metric")

write_csv(flagged_samples, file.path(output_dir, "flagged_samples_review.csv"))
write_csv(outlier_audit, file.path(output_dir, "all_measurements_with_flags.csv"))
```

**Review questions:** Do both rules identify the same samples? Does one sample have several flagged metrics? Could the result reflect a transcription error, technical artifact, or biologically meaningful extreme? What evidence would you need before excluding it?

### Why not automatically calculate outlier thresholds within each site?

The mussel study has only a few individuals per site. With roughly 4–6 mussels at a site, site-level quartiles and MAD estimates are unstable. Start with **metric-wide** flags, then inspect site context. Site-level flagging can be revisited when group sizes and the scientific question justify it.

```{r}
plot_outliers<- outlier_audit %>%
  filter(is.finite(value)) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = site_work, y = value, color = flag_any)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0), size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "gray50", `TRUE` = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Flagged measurements in site context", x = "Site number",
       y = "Measurement", color = "Flagged") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))

figures_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "output")
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "outlier_audit.png"),
       plot = plot_outliers, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

## Compare two retention scenarios

Both scenarios below retain the original untouched values in the audit:

- **All observations:** every finite measurement, including flagged values.
- **Flags excluded (sensitivity only):** finite measurements except those flagged for that **specific metric**.

**A sample flagged on P450 is still retained for SOD and shell unless those measurements are independently flagged.** This prevents accidental removal of complete mussels from the entire data set.

```{r}
scenario_data <- bind_rows(
  outlier_audit %>%
    filter(is.finite(value)) %>%
    mutate(scenario = "All observations"),
  outlier_audit %>%
    filter(is.finite(value), !sensitivity_exclude) %>%
    mutate(scenario = "Flags excluded (sensitivity only)")
)

scenario_counts <- scenario_data %>%
  count(metric, scenario, name = "n_included")
kable(scenario_counts)
```

## Apply fixed transformations

We show **raw**, **signed cube root** (valid for negative, zero, or positive numbers), **square root** (nonnegative only), **log1p** = log(1 + x) (x > −1), and **asinh** (all real numbers). The last is especially useful for teaching transformations that accept zero and negative values. These are examples, not a prescribed choice for every biomarker.

We apply the **same mathematical definition** to retained and excluded scenarios so comparisons are meaningful. Unlike a fitted Box–Cox or Tukey transformation, none of the formulas below is tuned separately to each scenario.

```{r}
transformed_data <- scenario_data %>%
  mutate(
    raw = value,
    signed_cuberoot = sign(value) * abs(value)^(1/3),
    square_root = if_else(value >= 0, sqrt(pmax(value, 0)), NA_real_),
    log1p_value = if_else(value > -1, log1p(value), NA_real_),
    asinh_value = asinh(value)
  ) %>%
  select(sample_id_work, site_work, metric, scenario,
         flag_any, raw, signed_cuberoot, square_root,
         log1p_value, asinh_value) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(raw, signed_cuberoot, square_root,
                        log1p_value, asinh_value),
               names_to = "transformation", values_to = "transformed_value")

transformation_availability <- transformed_data %>%
  group_by(metric, scenario, transformation) %>%
  summarise(n_finite = sum(is.finite(transformed_value)),
            n_undefined = sum(!is.finite(transformed_value)),
            .groups = "drop")
kable(transformation_availability)
```

**Caution on logs:** `log1p(x)` is a mathematically defined demonstration, not a universally justified biological offset. Its interpretation depends on the units and measurement scale. For conventional `log(x)`, strictly positive values are required. Never silently replace zero with an arbitrary tiny number without explaining and defending the choice.

### View histogram and Q–Q plot comparisons

```{r}
#| label: transformation-histograms
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Ensure the figures directory exists
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Retain only finite transformed values
hist_data <- transformed_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(metric),
         is.finite(transformed_value))

# Identify all available metrics
metric_list <- unique(hist_data$metric)

# Generate individual distribution plots by metric
for (m in metric_list) {

  # Subset data for the current metric
  metric_data <- hist_data %>%
    filter(metric == m)

  # Generate faceted histograms
  plot_transformedhist <- metric_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = transformed_value)) +
    geom_histogram(
      bins = 18,
      fill = "steelblue",
      color = "white"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(scenario, transformation),
      scales = "free",
      ncol = n_distinct(metric_data$transformation)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution assessment:", m),
      subtitle = "Original versus transformed distributions, with and without flags",
      x = "Value on indicated scale",
      y = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines")
    )

  # Save individual figure to the figures directory
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      figures_dir,
      paste0("transformations_hist_", m, ".png")
    ),
    plot = plot_transformedhist,
    width = 12,
    height = 6,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 300
  )

  # Display figure in the rendered report
  print(plot_transformedhist)
}
```

```{r}
# Ensure figures directory exists
#dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Identify all available metrics
metric_list <- unique(na.omit(transformed_data$metric))

# Generate individual Q-Q plots by metric
for (m in metric_list) {

  plot_transformedqq <- transformed_data %>%
    filter(metric == m,
           is.finite(transformed_value)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(sample = transformed_value)) +
    stat_qq(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
    stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(scenario, transformation),
      scales = "free",
      nrow = length(unique(na.omit(transformed_data$scenario)))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Transformation assessment:", m),
      subtitle = "Q-Q plots with and without flagged observations",
      x = "Theoretical quantiles",
      y = "Sample quantiles"
    ) +

    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),

    )

  # Save individual figure
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      figures_dir,
      paste0("transformations_qq_", m, ".png")

    plot = plot_transformedqq,
    width = 12,
    height = 6,
    dpi = 300
  )

  print(plot_transformedqq)
}
```

### Compare descriptive summaries

A transformation changes scale, so means and standard deviations on different transformed scales are **not directly comparable** in magnitude. Here we report n, median, IQR, and the sample skewness coefficient as descriptive aids, not as a decision rule.

```{r}
transformation_summary <- transformed_data %>%
  filter(is.finite(transformed_value)) %>%
  group_by(metric, scenario, transformation) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(transformed_value),
    sd = sd(transformed_value),
    median = median(transformed_value),
    iqr = IQR(transformed_value),
    skewness = if (n() >= 3 && sd(transformed_value) > 0)
      mean((transformed_value - mean(transformed_value))^3) /
      sd(transformed_value)^3 else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
kable(transformation_summary, digits = 3)
write_csv(transformation_summary,
          file.path(output_dir, "transformation_comparison_summary.csv"))
```

## 7. Create a decision log (do not remove records automatically)

The flagged observations have **not** been declared invalid. This review template is where a student documents independent evidence about an observation before exclusion from any primary analysis.

```{r}
decision_log <- flagged_samples %>%
  transmute(
    sample_id = sample_id_work,
    site_number = site_work,
    metric, observed_value = value,
    iqr_flag = flag_iqr,
    mad_flag = flag_mad,
    check_raw_file = "",
    check_protocol_or_instrument = "",
    check_site_and_biology = "",
    decision = "PENDING REVIEW",
    rationale = "",
    reviewer = "",
    review_date = ""
  )
write_csv(decision_log, file.path(output_dir, "outlier_decision_log_template.csv"))
kable(head(decision_log, 10), caption = "First ten rows of the review template")
```
